body:
I'll start by understanding the repository structure, the SKILL.md rules, and the reference style before writing.

Now I have enough verified source material. Writing the four chapters.

Now a targeted self-check of citations and fences without running the shared verifier.

Completed all four assigned chapters in `runtimes/podman_guide/`:

| File | Lines | Content |
|---|---:|---|
| `00-index.md` | 129 | Scope/baseline, invariants, measured surface (205 inventory pages, 136 captured, 12 samples, 10,516 repo files, 424 docs markdown — each labelled measured), full citation + fence contract with a verbatim example, concept map (7 required concepts + release tracks/determinism), read order with entry paths, explicit out-of-scope, 8-step refresh procedure |
| `01-product-and-architecture.md` | 120 | Daemonless model (verbatim `podman.1.md:4-14`), component map incl. v6 `go.podman.io/common` and `go.podman.io/storage` module paths, libpod/Buildah image-only sharing, OCI runtime + conmon with version floors, local/remote/machine topologies, v5.8 vs v6.2 with BoltDB removal, Quadlet/kube surfaces, graphroot/runroot/XDG state table |
| `02-installation-and-platforms.md` | 160 | Distro install matrix, macOS installer-vs-Homebrew verbatim excerpt, WSL2/machines, `podman info` verification queries, FreeBSD setup, source-build deps and full build-tag table, rootless prerequisites checklist, version-pinning channels with production verdicts |
| `03-rootless-and-userns.md` | 133 | Subuid/subgid ranges with two verbatim excerpts, full `--userns` key/mode tables (`auto`/`host`/`keep-id`/`nomap`/`ns`/`container`), deterministic volume UID mapping, pasta vs slirp4netns, cgroups v2 gates, `unshare`/`migrate` triggers, `subid: sss`, `ping_group_range`, limitations |

Verification performed: a local structural/citation check (first-line shape, `##` section count and final pair, line bounds, token file/range validity, fence language/verbatim equality, forbidden markers) — all four pass at 120–160 lines. `verify.py` was not run, per assignment.
